title: Remote Sessions skills and feature doc
body:
Teach agents and readers the finished feature: add a short "another PC" section using --on to the dispatch and chat skills (both providers' copies), write the feature doc with its gotchas and Key files, and add a pointer row in the agent guides if one is needed. Read the foreman-docs-and-writing skill first for the house style and the embedded-skill rebuild rule.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (whole file)
Blocked by: Launcher where-strip, directory prompt and split inheritance; Disconnect bar, reconnect and restore-disconnected; Tunnel listener: token, chat and status routes, reply note
Done when:
- the skill sections say when to use --on versus --host, and that a Remote agent can post chat but cannot open, send or close
- the Claude and Codex skill copies agree, and the rebuild rule for embedded skills is followed
- the feature doc records only gotchas, whys and procedures, cites symbols not line numbers, and passes the cite guard
Notes from landed cards (read `git log --oneline 4aa5a53..HEAD` for what shipped):
- This card runs BEFORE the hooks card (sfyaz0), which is waiting on a Claude login on the test Remote. Do not claim agent-state badges work on a Remote Session; say they are not available yet and leave one line for sfyaz0 to update. Everything else has landed.
- Record these gotchas and whys, each only if the code does not already say it: the Tunnel token is per connection and renewed on reconnect; the forwarded port is reachable by every user on the Remote, and slots are shared across Remotes; a reply refused before its request is read must drain or Windows resets the connection (already in foreman-debugging-playbook, point at it, do not repeat it); reconnect never replays the original argv and a wrapped agent relaunches bare; resume drops the original --model and permission flags; Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot pass some arguments and the builder refuses them; the launch reply note can land in an ssh password prompt because Ready latches on first output; file-path links and file drops do not exist yet, so nothing gates them on a Remote Session; every Windows-Remote claim is untested (no Windows Remote exists) and must be labelled so.
- A Remote agent may post chat, read history, read status and report hook events. It may not open, send to, close or snapshot panes, or use the kanban board. Say exactly this in the skills.
- The reply command for a Remote agent is in the reply note it receives; the skills should tell a dispatcher that `open --on R -- claude "<brief>"` gets that note at launch.
Gate: pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All; cargo test --target-dir target/agent skills
